1→# 47 Entire CLI UX vs Doraval

**Captured:** 2026-08-20
**Status:** research only. Do not edit Doraval CLI from this file.
**Bar product:** [entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli) live `0.10.1` + clone HEAD `91a7fd7`
**Library (no Entire dep):** OpenTUI — https://opentui.com/ (repo [anomalyco/opentui](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui), MIT)
**Sibling:** [`46-agent-browser-cli-ux.md`](./46-agent-browser-cli-ux.md) (same rubric)

This note is CLI surface only: `--help`, flags, output, errors, TUI, doctor/install, agent-help, MCP, hooks.
10→
**Correction:** Entire does **not** use OpenTUI. Entire is Go + Cobra + Charm (`huh`, Bubble Tea). OpenTUI is a separate TypeScript/Zig kit used by OpenCode. Doraval can adopt OpenTUI with no Entire dependency. This note still ranks OpenTUI on its own merits.

---

## 0. Method

Cloned `https://github.com/entireio/cli` shallow on 2026-08-20 to `/tmp/entire-cli-research`. HEAD `91a7fd7` (“Merge pull request #2045…”). Read `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (`AGENTS.md` is a symlink), `cmd/entire/main.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/root.go`, `help.go`, `agent_help_cmd.go`, `doctor.go`, `errors.go`, `mcp.go`, `status.go`, `setup.go`, `setup_agent_help_skill.go`, `progress.go`, `uiform/uiform.go`, `interactive/interactive.go`, `experimental/experimental.go`, `agent/cursor/hooks.go`, `go.mod`.

Did **not** run `entire enable` / `entire install` in `/Users/saif/Experiments/doraval`. Friction log (`docs/friction-log.md`) says enable writes hooks and dirties `git status`. Source confirms that. Live binary was already on PATH (`/Users/saif/.local/bin/entire`). Ran read-only help from `/tmp`:
20→
```bash
entire version          # 0.10.1
entire --help
entire agent-help
entire agent-help --json
entire agent-help status
entire doctor --help
entire enable --help
entire status --help
30→entire status --json    # from /tmp: not a git repo
entire session --help
entire checkpoint --help
entire search --help
entire labs --help
entire completion --help
entire nosuch
```

Doraval: read `src/cli/*` in this repo (v0.6.18). Ran:
40→
```bash
bun run src/cli/index.ts --help
bun run src/cli/index.ts review --help
bun run src/cli/index.ts scan --help
bun run src/cli/index.ts fix --help
bun run src/cli/index.ts reconcile --help
bun run src/cli/index.ts nosuch
```

50→First-party docs: `https://docs.entire.io` works. `https://entire.io/docs` redirected to `https://entire.io/login?next=/docs` (not a 404; not public CLI docs). `https://entire.io` is marketing. Used docs only for CLI behavior.

OpenTUI: https://opentui.com/, https://opentui.com/docs/, https://opentui.com/docs/components/, https://opentui.com/docs/getting-started/runtime-support/, https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui, MIT LICENSE raw.

Confirmed `@opentui/*` is **not** in Doraval `package.json`. Leftover `node_modules/@opentui/core@0.4.2` exists. Do not treat it as a product dependency.

---

## 1. Entire CLI surface (inventory)

60→One Go binary. Cobra (`github.com/spf13/cobra`). Prompts: Charm `huh` (`charm.land/huh/v2`). Full-screen views: Bubble Tea (`charm.land/bubbletea/v2`). Not citty. Not OpenTUI. Not Ink. Source: `CLAUDE.md` L7; `go.mod` L5–9, L40.

| Surface | What it is | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bare / `--help` / `-h` | Grouped catalog + Getting Started | `root.go` `gettingStarted`, `NewRootCmd` |
| Bare in unset git repo | Starts setup (`runSetupFlow`) | `root.go` L95–101 |
| `<cmd> --help` | Cobra Long + Examples + flags | live `entire session --help`, `search --help` |
| `agent-help [command…]` | Live agent usage from the Cobra tree | `agent_help_cmd.go` `newAgentHelpCmd` |
| `--version` / `-v` / `version` | Version, Go, OS/Arch | `root.go` `versionString`; live `0.10.1` |
| `enable` / `disable` / `status` | First loop + health | README Quick Start; `setup.go` |
70→| `doctor` | Stuck sessions + hook drift; `--force` | `doctor.go`; https://docs.entire.io/cli-reference/doctor.md |
| `doctor logs \| bundle \| trace` | Logs, redacted zip, hook traces | `doctor.go` L75–78 |
| `agent add/remove/list` | Install hooks per agent | README; `setup.go` |
| `session` / `checkpoint` / `search` | Session record (not Doraval transcripts) | `CLAUDE.md` Command Layout |
| `login` / `auth` / `org` / `repo` | Account + control plane | `root.go` groups |
| `mcp` | Hidden stdio MCP: `agent_help` + `entire_status` | `mcp.go` L41–54 |
| `completion bash\|zsh\|fish\|powershell` | Hidden cobra default | `root.go` `HiddenDefaultCmd: true`; live `entire completion --help` |
| Plugins | `entire-<name>` on PATH, kubectl-style | README Plugins; `main.go` `MaybeRunPlugin` |
| Experimental | `review`, `investigate`, `why`, `blame`, `experts`, … | `experimental.Register`; `entire labs` |
| Hidden infra | `hooks`, `trail`, `__send_analytics`, `curl-bash-post-install` | `root.go` L153–158; `CLAUDE.md` L163–165 |
80→
Help groups in live `entire --help` (order): Entire Setup → Sessions & Checkpoints → Account → Control Plane → Additional Commands (`agent-help`, `help`, `labs`, `version`). Source: `root.go` L35–43, L107–113.

Stable release hides experimental commands from human help (`experimental.Visible` stamped `"false"`). They stay runnable. `agent-help` still listed `why` on this 0.10.1 binary. Source: `experimental/experimental.go` L1–17.

`--json` is **per-command**, not a global root flag. Live root flags are `--context`, `-h`, `-v` only. Docs: https://docs.entire.io/cli-reference/global-flags.md.

---

## 2. Help and first-loop UX
90→
### Entire top-level `--help`

Opens **Reader-first**, then a first command. Quoted from live `entire --help` (`root.go` `gettingStarted` + `accessibilityHelp`):

```
The command-line interface for Entire

Getting Started:
  To get started with Entire CLI, run 'entire enable' to enable
100→  session tracking in your repository, then 'entire agent add <name>'
  to install hooks for a specific agent. For more information, visit:
  https://docs.entire.io/overview

Environment Variables:
  ACCESSIBLE    Set to any value (e.g., ACCESSIBLE=1) to enable accessibility
                mode. This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive
                TUI elements, which works better with screen readers.
```

110→Then: grouped verb catalog → Flags (`--context`, `-h`, `-v`).

**Length:** ~65 lines. Grouped. Not an encyclopedia. Better size than agent-browser’s ~390-line catalog (note 46). Longer than Doraval’s 32-line flat list.

**Env vars in help:** only `ACCESSIBLE`. Other env (`ENTIRE_TOKEN`, `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`, `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL`) live in README / docs, not top-level help.

**Examples:** none on the root page. The opener *is* the next command.

### Entire per-command `--help`

120→Cobra. Typical shape (`session`, `checkpoint`, `search`, `doctor`):

1. Long prose (what + gotchas)
2. `Commands:` / `Examples:` block
3. Usage
4. Available Commands
5. Flags + Global Flags
6. “Use `entire <cmd> --help` …”

`entire session --help` has eight copy-paste examples, including `--json`. `entire search --help` documents `--json` / `--compact` and the non-TTY rule (“Run without arguments to open an interactive search… Use `--json` for machine-readable output”). `entire doctor --help` lists checks, `--force`, and subcommands. That matches note 46’s “doctor is the best recovery page.”
130→
`agent-help <cmd>` is a **second** per-command page for agents: Short, Long, “When to use this,” Examples, live Flags, Subcommands, `Next: entire agent-help …`. Source: `renderAgentHelpCommand` in `agent_help_cmd.go` L576–628.

### Doraval top-level `--help` (citty default)

Ran `bun run src/cli/index.ts --help` (32 lines). Banner from `src/cli/index.ts` `meta.description`:

```
Reads your repo and tells you what's broken in agent context.
Primary: scan · review · fix · new --for <agent>.
140→Tip: point a coding agent at this CLI, or run `dora` (scan). Docs: https://doraval.dev
```

Then citty `USAGE` + `OPTIONS` + flat `COMMANDS` (12 names). No groups. `command-tree.ts` comments “primary” vs “tooling”; citty does not show that.

**Voice:** Reader-ish (human tip + docs URL). Same gap as note 46: `--help` never says `review --quick`. [`CONTEXT.md`](../../CONTEXT.md): top-level help is Reader. First loop is `npx skills add` then `dora review --quick`.

**Missing vs Entire:** grouped catalog, a runnable “Start here” pair, per-command examples. Entire’s ~65-line grouped help is the better size target if Doraval adds groups — not agent-browser’s encyclopedia.

Test pin: `test/cli.test.ts` `--help lists core commands` asserts `Primary:`, `point a coding agent`, `https://doraval.dev`, and that root blurbs stay short.
150→
### Doraval per-command `--help`

Citty only. `dora review --help` is 22 lines: description + USAGE + OPTIONS. No examples. No exit-code table. No “then run `dora fix`”. `--deep` / `--sessions` mention “exit 2” in the flag blurb. That is the only exit teaching in `--help`.

`dora scan --help` is 12 lines. `dora fix --help` has `--brief` / `--yes` / `--dry-run` but no example lines. `dora reconcile --help` documents `--apply` / `--dry-run` / `--yes` and does **not** say those are the agent path.

Runtime *does* teach next steps (`nextAction` in `out.ts`; scan “Next” suggestions; review → `dora fix`). That teaching is after a run, not in `--help`.

### First loop from the CLI itself
160→
| | Entire | Doraval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| From `--help` alone | Yes. “Getting Started” → `entire enable` then `entire agent add <name>`. Docs URL. | Partial. Banner says run `dora` (scan). Does not name `dora review --quick`. |
| Doctor / install | `doctor` is recovery, not first run. First run is `enable`. | No `doctor`. `dora update` ≈ upgrade. Scan embeds platform-install check. |
| Skill from CLI | Opt-in `--agent-help-skill` writes a stub that points at `entire agent-help`. Default enable installs no skill. | No `dora skills get`. Shipped skill `skills/doraval/SKILL.md` is the teacher. First Review is `dora review --quick`. |
| Agent map from CLI | `entire agent-help` (visible in help). `status` footer: `Agents: run \`entire agent-help\``. | `--capabilities` (3 of 12 commands). Scan “Next” is human commands, not the machine manifest. |
| Bare binary | Unset git repo → setup wizard. Else help. | Bare `dora` **is** scan (`index.ts` L86–88). TTY confirm unless `--yes` / `--format json`. |

An agent that only has `entire --help` learns `enable` then `agent add`. An agent that only has `dora --help` does **not** learn the CONTEXT.md first loop. Same gap as note 46.
170→
`agent-help` is Entire’s real agent teacher. It classifies commands as `read-only` / `task-driven` / `user-owned` and tells agents not to run `enable` / `review` / `org` unprompted. Source: `agentHelpClassification` in `agent_help_cmd.go` L97–179. Doraval’s equivalent is `--capabilities`, not a new verb.

---

## 3. Output, JSON, TTY, exit codes

### Entire

Default is **pretty text** on stdout. Many verbs open a TUI when stdout is a TTY (`activity` → `runActivityTUI`; `search` with no query → interactive table). Non-TTY or `ACCESSIBLE` falls back to static text. Source: `activity_cmd.go` L67–72; `search_cmd.go` Long; `CLAUDE.md` § Agent-Safe CLI Fallbacks L766–814.
180→
`--json` is **per-command**. Not a root flag. Commands that have it: `status`, `agent-help`, `session list/info`, `search` (`--compact` implies `--json`), `checkpoint list/explain`, trail finding, `experts`. Source: `CLAUDE.md` L775–810; live `--help` pages.

JSON goes to **stdout**. Version-upgrade notice is forced to **stderr** so it cannot corrupt `--json` pipes. Source: `root.go` L88–93 (`PersistentPostRun`); live `entire version` printed the update block after the version lines.

`--compact` (search): trimmed agent shape (id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files, score, snippet, truncated title). Implies `--json`. Source: live `entire search --help`; `search_cmd.go` L53–58.

Color: Charm / `ShouldStyle`. `NO_COLOR` wins. Non-TTY and `TERM=cygwin` skip ANSI. Source: `interactive.go` `ShouldStyle` L110–117.

Progress: custom spinner on stdout/err with 250 ms delay; no frames when the writer is not a styled TTY. Source: `progress.go` L24–47.
190→
Exit codes: almost always **0 or 1**. `main.go` `os.Exit(1)` on error. Signals: SIGINT → 130, SIGTERM → 143 (`dieFromSignal`). Help/version return 0. No “could not run” = 2. `status` treats “not a git repo” as status text, exit 0 (`status.go` L63–65).

## 5. TUI and OpenTUI (Entire vs Doraval render/clack)

### Does Entire use OpenTUI?

**No.** Grep over `/tmp/entire-cli-research` for `opentui` / `@opentui` / `OpenTUI`: zero hits. `go.mod` requires Charm, not OpenTUI. `CLAUDE.md` L7: “CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh”.

### What Entire’s TUI actually does
260→
Two layers:

1. **Prompts (huh).** Confirm, select, multi-select, text. Wrapped in `uiform.New` / `NewAccessibleForm` so `ACCESSIBLE` switches to simpler text. Used by `enable`, `clean`, `session` pickers, `repo` wizards, `attach`. Source: `uiform/uiform.go`; `setup.go` `hookAgentOptions`; `sessions.go` MultiSelect; `resume_picker.go`.

2. **Full-screen apps (Bubble Tea).** `activity` (default TTY), `search` (no-query TTY), `recap`, `dispatch`, `investigate` live view, `experts --tui` (opt-in). These are dashboards / browsers over hosted session data. Not one-shot CLI prompts.

CLAUDE.md L766–814 is the important rule: **do not hide useful output behind a TUI.** Every TUI path must have list+show, a flag, or a text/JSON fallback. `experts --tui` is called out as safe because it is opt-in and non-TTY is plain text.

`CanPromptInteractively` (`interactive.go`): off in `go test`, `CI`, agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`), and when `/dev/tty` is raw (lazygit parent). Doraval already skips clack when stdin/stderr are not TTY (`prompt.ts`, `shouldConfirmScan`, `shouldAskReviewLimit`). Doraval does not special-case those agent env vars.

### What OpenTUI actually provides

From https://opentui.com/ and https://opentui.com/docs/:

- Native Zig core + TypeScript bindings. Flexbox (Yoga). Component tree.
- Packages: `@opentui/core` (imperative), `@opentui/react`, `@opentui/solid`, plus keymap / qrcode / ssh / three.
- Powers **OpenCode**, not Entire.
- License: MIT (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opentui/main/LICENSE). Official repo is [anomalyco/opentui](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui) (site still mentions sst in older links).

280→Components (https://opentui.com/docs/components/): Text, Box, Input, Textarea, Select, TabSelect, Slider, ScrollBox, Code, Markdown, Diff, TextTable, Image, QR, embedded terminal. **No Confirm. No Spinner.** That is a full-screen app kit, not a clack replacement.

Runtime (https://opentui.com/docs/getting-started/runtime-support/): Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (Doraval already requires this). Node.js “26.4.0 exactly” + `--experimental-ffi`. Native optionalDeps per platform (same pattern as Doraval’s own binaries). Adding `@opentui/core` is a new native dep + platform packages.

Leftover in this tree: `node_modules/@opentui/core@0.4.2` and `core-darwin-x64`. **Not** in `package.json` `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. A prior look only. Do not treat as adopted.

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |

| scan, review, fix, reconcile, config, rules, bump, memory/* | clack for TTY gates |

Commands use `ui.*` from `out.ts`. They never call the interface. A second backend would have to reimplement line-oriented helpers (`heading`, `failItem`), not OpenTUI’s box/flex tree. **This is a text seam, not a TUI seam.**

## 3. Output, JSON, TTY, exit codes

### Entire

Default is **pretty text** on stdout. Many verbs open a TUI when stdout is a TTY (`activity` → `runActivityTUI`; `search` with no query → interactive table). Non-TTY or `ACCESSIBLE` falls back to static text. Source: `activity_cmd.go` L67–72; `search_cmd.go` Long; `CLAUDE.md` § Agent-Safe CLI Fallbacks L766–814.
180→
`--json` is **per-command**. Not a root flag. Commands that have it: `status`, `agent-help`, `session list/info`, `search` (`--compact` implies `--json`), `checkpoint list/explain`, trail finding, `experts`. Source: `CLAUDE.md` L775–810; live `--help` pages.

JSON goes to **stdout**. Version-upgrade notice is forced to **stderr** so it cannot corrupt `--json` pipes. Source: `root.go` L88–93 (`PersistentPostRun`); live `entire version` printed the update block after the version lines.

`--compact` (search): trimmed agent shape (id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files, score, snippet, truncated title). Implies `--json`. Source: live `entire search --help`; `search_cmd.go` L53–58.

Color: Charm / `ShouldStyle`. `NO_COLOR` wins. Non-TTY and `TERM=cygwin` skip ANSI. Source: `interactive.go` `ShouldStyle` L110–117.

Progress: custom spinner on stdout/err with 250 ms delay; no frames when the writer is not a styled TTY. Source: `progress.go` L24–47.
190→
Exit codes: almost always **0 or 1**. `main.go` `os.Exit(1)` on error. Signals: SIGINT → 130, SIGTERM → 143 (`dieFromSignal`). Help/version return 0. No “could not run” = 2. `status` treats “not a git repo” as status text, exit 0 (`status.go` L63–65).

Unknown command: reprints **full root usage** on stderr, then `Error: Invalid usage: unknown command "nosuch" for "entire"`. Source: `main.go` `showSuggestion` L203–207; live `entire nosuch`. Same noise class as citty. Worse than agent-browser’s one-liner (note 46).

### Doraval

Default is **table** (pretty) on **stderr** via `text-backend.ts`. JSON data is **stdout** (`outJson`). JSON **errors** are **stderr** (`emitError`). `--ci` implies `--format json` (`resolveOutputMode`).

This split is better for pipes than Entire’s “pretty and JSON both on stdout.” Keep it. Do not copy Entire’s stdout-for-humans model.
200→
`--format json` vs Entire `--json`: Doraval is more explicit (table | json) and global. No `--json` alias. No `--compact`. Skill tells agents to add `--format json` after a `--quick` pass.

Progress: `preflight.ts` gates stage lines; silent in JSON. Spinners and confirms write to **stderr**. Good.

Color: picocolors on TTY. `NO_COLOR` is the usual disable. No “color off unless opted in.” `--ci` / JSON skip the pretty path.

Exit codes (skill + `capabilities.ts` `EXIT_CODES`):

| Code | Meaning |
210→| --- | --- |
| 0 | clean |
| 1 | issues found |
| 2 | could not run (internal / unmet prerequisite) |

`--deep` with no judge → 2. Stronger contract than Entire. Keep it.

Stable IDs: review findings use `R0xx` when coded. Scan health uses `E-SCAN-*`. Entire uses checkpoint hex IDs and session `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>`. Different objects. Do not copy.

## 4. Errors and recovery

### Entire failed command

`main.go`: if the command did not already print (`SilentError`), print `RenderUserFacingError` on stderr and exit 1. That helper only strips OpenAPI `BearerAuth` wrapping (`errors.go` L4–20). No `Context:` / `Solutions:` / `Next:` shape.

Unknown command / unknown flag / bad args: dump `UsageString()` then `Error: Invalid usage: …` (`showSuggestion`). **Does reprint help.**

Doctor (`doctor.go`): scan-and-fix for **sessions** — disconnected metadata branches, git hooks, Codex hook trust, hook-config drift, stuck ACTIVE/ENDED sessions. `--force` auto-condenses or discards. Subcommands: `logs`, `bundle` (redacted zip), `trace`, `migrate-checkpoints`. This is session-store recovery, not “is the CLI installed.”
230→
Status is the light health verb: `○ not set up (run \`entire enable\`)` / enabled + agent-help footer (`status.go` L90–111).

Update: `PersistentPostRun` calls `versioncheck.CheckAndNotify` (24 h cache, stderr). Live `entire version` printed `Update available! 0.10.1 -> 0.10.2` and `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`. Docs: https://docs.entire.io/updating.md. `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` disables prompts.

### Doraval failed command

`guidedError` (`out.ts`): `Error:` → `Context:` → `Solutions:` bullets → optional `Docs:` → `Next:`. `emitError` wraps `DoravalError` the same way, or JSON `{error:{code,message,suggestion,docUrl,context}}` on stderr.

This already beats Entire’s one-line (or usage-dump) errors for humans and agents.
240→
Unknown command (citty `runMain`): full 32-line `--help` on **stdout**, `Unknown command nosuch` on **stderr**, exit **1**. Entire does the same dump. Agent-browser does not. Prefer the one-liner from note 46, not Entire.

No `dora doctor`. Closest pieces:

- Bare scan + Intelligence `install` (`src/core/platform-install.ts`). Local only.
- `dora update` ≈ Entire’s upgrade notice + install.sh (detect homebrew | npm | bun).
- Scan / review “Next” lists after a successful run.

Doraval does not need session condensation or hook-trust repair. A copy of `entire doctor` would be empty. Scan already is the health command.
250→

## 5. TUI and OpenTUI (Entire vs Doraval render/clack)

### Does Entire use OpenTUI?

**No.** Grep over `/tmp/entire-cli-research` for `opentui` / `@opentui` / `OpenTUI`: zero hits. `go.mod` requires Charm, not OpenTUI. `CLAUDE.md` L7: “CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh”.

### What Entire’s TUI actually does
260→
Two layers:

1. **Prompts (huh).** Confirm, select, multi-select, text. Wrapped in `uiform.New` / `NewAccessibleForm` so `ACCESSIBLE` switches to simpler text. Used by `enable`, `clean`, `session` pickers, `repo` wizards, `attach`. Source: `uiform/uiform.go`; `setup.go` `hookAgentOptions`; `sessions.go` MultiSelect; `resume_picker.go`.

2. **Full-screen apps (Bubble Tea).** `activity` (default TTY), `search` (no-query TTY), `recap`, `dispatch`, `investigate` live view, `experts --tui` (opt-in). These are dashboards / browsers over hosted session data. Not one-shot CLI prompts.

CLAUDE.md L766–814 is the important rule: **do not hide useful output behind a TUI.** Every TUI path must have list+show, a flag, or a text/JSON fallback. `experts --tui` is called out as safe because it is opt-in and non-TTY is plain text.

`CanPromptInteractively` (`interactive.go`): off in `go test`, `CI`, agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`), and when `/dev/tty` is raw (lazygit parent). Doraval already skips clack when stdin/stderr are not TTY (`prompt.ts`, `shouldConfirmScan`, `shouldAskReviewLimit`). Doraval does not special-case those agent env vars.
270→
### What OpenTUI actually provides

From https://opentui.com/ and https://opentui.com/docs/:

- Native Zig core + TypeScript bindings. Flexbox (Yoga). Component tree.
- Packages: `@opentui/core` (imperative), `@opentui/react`, `@opentui/solid`, plus keymap / qrcode / ssh / three.
- Powers **OpenCode**, not Entire.
- License: MIT (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opentui/main/LICENSE). Official repo is [anomalyco/opentui](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui) (site still mentions sst in older links).

280→Components (https://opentui.com/docs/components/): Text, Box, Input, Textarea, Select, TabSelect, Slider, ScrollBox, Code, Markdown, Diff, TextTable, Image, QR, embedded terminal. **No Confirm. No Spinner.** That is a full-screen app kit, not a clack replacement.

Runtime (https://opentui.com/docs/getting-started/runtime-support/): Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (Doraval already requires this). Node.js “26.4.0 exactly” + `--experimental-ffi`. Native optionalDeps per platform (same pattern as Doraval’s own binaries). Adding `@opentui/core` is a new native dep + platform packages.

Leftover in this tree: `node_modules/@opentui/core@0.4.2` and `core-darwin-x64`. **Not** in `package.json` `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. A prior look only. Do not treat as adopted.

### Doraval today

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |
290→| `@clack/prompts` | confirm / select / text / password / spinner / multiselect. Already in `package.json`. |
| `src/cli/prompt.ts` | text + select; non-TTY returns fallback; chrome on stderr |
| scan, review, fix, reconcile, config, rules, bump, memory/* | clack for TTY gates |
| `memory/stash-picker.ts` | clack multiselect (cap 20) or optional `fzf` |
| `src/cli/render/backend.ts` | `RenderBackend` interface: write/info/dim/heading/success/warn/fail + `destroy()` |
| `render/text-backend.ts` | the only implementation; human UI on stderr |
| `render/index.ts` | “Text-only since the OpenTUI stack was removed — the indirection stays so exit.ts and out.ts keep a single seam.” |
| `render/exit.ts` | destroy backend then exit; backstop on `process.exit` |

`backend.ts` comment: “keep this seam; a second (TUI/dashboard) backend was removed and may return as dora ui.” That is a leftover from a removed dashboard, not a planned OpenTUI adapter. Commands use `ui.*` from `out.ts`. They never call the interface. A second backend would have to reimplement line-oriented helpers (`heading`, `failItem`), not OpenTUI’s box/flex tree. **This is a text seam, not a TUI seam.**
300→
### Rank (YAGNI)

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Stay on clack | **Yes.** Confirm/select/spinner/multiselect already match every Doraval TTY gate. |
| OpenTUI for one surface | **No.** Scan table, review findings, reconcile picker, stash picker are not worse than Entire’s huh pickers in a way OpenTUI would fix. OpenTUI has no confirm/spinner. It is the wrong layer. |
| Skip TUI entirely | **Yes for dashboards.** Entire’s Bubble Tea views are activity/search/recap over hosted sessions. Doraval has no equivalent command. A `dora ui` dashboard is speculative. |

**OpenTUI verdict:** do not add `@opentui/*`. Entire does not use it. It is a full-app kit. Clack + `text-backend` already cover scan / review / fix / reconcile / stash. If a later command needs a full-screen browser, that is Adapt and a new dep — not Copy now.
310→

## 6. Agent-native extras (hooks, MCP, capabilities)

### `agent-help` (describe, then Adapt as `--capabilities`, not a new verb)

`entire agent-help` prints a curated map live from the installed Cobra tree. Bare: overview + repo line + listed commands with audience + footer of the rest + “Drill in… `--json`”. Drill: flags + examples + `Next:`. `--json` emits `{command, short, long, flags, subcommands[], audience}`. Source: `agent_help_cmd.go`; https://docs.entire.io/cli-reference/agent-help.md.

Audience policy: `read-only` (safe unprompted), `task-driven` (writes / spends tokens), `user-owned` (setup/auth — suggest, don’t run). Unclassified → user-owned, unlisted. CI requires every advertised command to be classified. Source: `agentHelpClassification`; `CLAUDE.md` L123–137.
320→
Discovery for agents without a hook channel: visible in `entire help`; `status` footer; `status --json` field `agent_help`; Factory Droid SessionStart banner; hidden `entire mcp` tools. Source: `CLAUDE.md` L149–157; `status.go` `writeAgentHelpHint` L123–128; `statusJSON.AgentHelp` L750–753.

Optional `--agent-help-skill` writes a **near-immutable stub** into the user’s repo (`.claude/skills/entire/SKILL.md`, `.codex/agents/entire.toml`, `.gemini/agents/entire.md`) that only says “run `entire agent-help`.” Default enable does **not** install it. Source: `setup_agent_help_skill.go` L22–26, L153–154 (test name: “opt-in only”).

**Voice:** Reader-ish (human tip + docs URL). Same gap as note 46: `--help` never says `review --quick`. [`CONTEXT.md`](../../CONTEXT.md): top-level help is Reader. First loop is `npx skills add` then `dora review --quick`.

**Missing vs Entire:** grouped catalog, a runnable “Start here” pair, per-command examples. Entire’s ~65-line grouped help is the better size target if Doraval adds groups — not agent-browser’s encyclopedia.

Test pin: `test/cli.test.ts` `--help lists core commands` asserts `Primary:`, `point a coding agent`, `https://doraval.dev`, and that root blurbs stay short.

### Doraval per-command `--help`

Citty only. `dora review --help` is 22 lines: description + USAGE + OPTIONS. No examples. No exit-code table. No “then run `dora fix`”. `--deep` / `--sessions` mention “exit 2” in the flag blurb. That is the only exit teaching in `--help`.

`dora scan --help` is 12 lines. `dora fix --help` has `--brief` / `--yes` / `--dry-run` but no example lines. `dora reconcile --help` documents `--apply` / `--dry-run` / `--yes` and does **not** say those are the agent path.

Runtime *does* teach next steps (`nextAction` in `out.ts`; scan “Next” suggestions; review → `dora fix`). That teaching is after a run, not in `--help`.

### First loop from the CLI itself

| | Entire | Doraval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| From `--help` alone | Yes. “Getting Started” → `entire enable` then `entire agent add <name>`. Docs URL. | Partial. Banner says run `dora` (scan). Does not name `dora review --quick`. |
| Doctor / install | `doctor` is recovery, not first run. First run is `enable`. | No `doctor`. `dora update` ≈ upgrade. Scan embeds platform-install check. |
| Skill from CLI | Opt-in `--agent-help-skill` writes a stub that points at `entire agent-help`. Default enable installs no skill. | No `dora skills get`. Shipped skill `skills/doraval/SKILL.md` is the teacher. First Review is `dora review --quick`. |
| Agent map from CLI | `entire agent-help` (visible in help). `status` footer: `Agents: run \`entire agent-help\``. | `--capabilities` (3 of 12 commands). Scan “Next” is human commands, not the machine manifest. |
| Bare binary | Unset git repo → setup wizard. Else help. | Bare `dora` **is** scan (`index.ts` L86–88). TTY confirm unless `--yes` / `--format json`. |

An agent that only has `entire --help` learns `enable` then `agent add`. An agent that only has `dora --help` does **not** learn the CONTEXT.md first loop. Same gap as note 46.

`agent-help` is Entire’s real agent teacher. It classifies commands as `read-only` / `task-driven` / `user-owned` and tells agents not to run `enable` / `review` / `org` unprompted. Source: `agentHelpClassification` in `agent_help_cmd.go` L97–179. Doraval’s equivalent is `--capabilities`, not a new verb.

## 3. Output, JSON, TTY, exit codes

### Entire

Default is **pretty text** on stdout. Many verbs open a TUI when stdout is a TTY (`activity` → `runActivityTUI`; `search` with no query → interactive table). Non-TTY or `ACCESSIBLE` falls back to static text. Source: `activity_cmd.go` L67–72; `search_cmd.go` Long; `CLAUDE.md` § Agent-Safe CLI Fallbacks L766–814.

`--json` is **per-command**. Not a root flag. Commands that have it: `status`, `agent-help`, `session list/info`, `search` (`--compact` implies `--json`), `checkpoint list/explain`, trail finding, `experts`. Source: `CLAUDE.md` L775–810; live `--help` pages.

JSON goes to **stdout**. Version-upgrade notice is forced to **stderr** so it cannot corrupt `--json` pipes. Source: `root.go` L88–93 (`PersistentPostRun`); live `entire version` printed the update block after the version lines.

`--compact` (search): trimmed agent shape (id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files, score, snippet, truncated title). Implies `--json`. Source: live `entire search --help`; `search_cmd.go` L53–58.

Color: Charm / `ShouldStyle`. `NO_COLOR` wins. Non-TTY and `TERM=cygwin` skip ANSI. Source: `interactive.go` `ShouldStyle` L110–117.

Progress: custom spinner on stdout/err with 250 ms delay; no frames when the writer is not a styled TTY. Source: `progress.go` L24–47.

Exit codes: almost always **0 or 1**. `main.go` `os.Exit(1)` on error. Signals: SIGINT → 130, SIGTERM → 143 (`dieFromSignal`). Help/version return 0. No “could not run” = 2. `status` treats “not a git repo” as status text, exit 0 (`status.go` L63–65).

Unknown command: reprints **full root usage** on stderr, then `Error: Invalid usage: unknown command "nosuch" for "entire"`. Source: `main.go` `showSuggestion` L203–207; live `entire nosuch`. Same noise class as citty. Worse than agent-browser’s one-liner (note 46).

### Doraval

Default is **table** (pretty) on **stderr** via `text-backend.ts`. JSON data is **stdout** (`outJson`). JSON **errors** are **stderr** (`emitError`). `--ci` implies `--format json` (`resolveOutputMode`).

This split is better for pipes than Entire’s “pretty and JSON both on stdout.” Keep it. Do not copy Entire’s stdout-for-humans model.

`--format json` vs Entire `--json`: Doraval is more explicit (table | json) and global. No `--json` alias. No `--compact`. Skill tells agents to add `--format json` after a `--quick` pass.

Progress: `preflight.ts` gates stage lines; silent in JSON. Spinners and confirms write to **stderr**. Good.

Color: picocolors on TTY. `NO_COLOR` is the usual disable. No “color off unless opted in.” `--ci` / JSON skip the pretty path.

Exit codes (skill + `capabilities.ts` `EXIT_CODES`):

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | clean |
| 1 | issues found |
| 2 | could not run (internal / unmet prerequisite) |

`--deep` with no judge → 2. Stronger contract than Entire. Keep it.

Stable IDs: review findings use `R0xx` when coded. Scan health uses `E-SCAN-*`. Entire uses checkpoint hex IDs and session `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>`. Different objects. Do not copy.

## 4. Errors and recovery

### Entire failed command

`main.go`: if the command did not already print (`SilentError`), print `RenderUserFacingError` on stderr and exit 1. That helper only strips OpenAPI `BearerAuth` wrapping (`errors.go` L4–20). No `Context:` / `Solutions:` / `Next:` shape.

Unknown command / unknown flag / bad args: dump `UsageString()` then `Error: Invalid usage: …` (`showSuggestion`). **Does reprint help.**

Doctor (`doctor.go`): scan-and-fix for **sessions** — disconnected metadata branches, git hooks, Codex hook trust, hook-config drift, stuck ACTIVE/ENDED sessions. `--force` auto-condenses or discards. Subcommands: `logs`, `bundle` (redacted zip), `trace`, `migrate-checkpoints`. This is session-store recovery, not “is the CLI installed.”

Status is the light health verb: `○ not set up (run \`entire enable\`)` / enabled + agent-help footer (`status.go` L90–111).

Update: `PersistentPostRun` calls `versioncheck.CheckAndNotify` (24 h cache, stderr). Live `entire version` printed `Update available! 0.10.1 -> 0.10.2` and `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`. Docs: https://docs.entire.io/updating.md. `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` disables prompts.

### Doraval failed command

`guidedError` (`out.ts`): `Error:` → `Context:` → `Solutions:` bullets → optional `Docs:` → `Next:`. `emitError` wraps `DoravalError` the same way, or JSON `{error:{code,message,suggestion,docUrl,context}}` on stderr.

This already beats Entire’s one-line (or usage-dump) errors for humans and agents.

Unknown command (citty `runMain`): full 32-line `--help` on **stdout**, `Unknown command nosuch` on **stderr**, exit **1**. Entire does the same dump. Agent-browser does not. Prefer the one-liner from note 46, not Entire.

No `dora doctor`. Closest pieces:

- Bare scan + Intelligence `install` (`src/core/platform-install.ts`). Local only.
- `dora update` ≈ Entire’s upgrade notice + install.sh (detect homebrew | npm | bun).
- Scan / review “Next” lists after a successful run.

Doraval does not need session condensation or hook-trust repair. A copy of `entire doctor` would be empty. Scan already is the health command.

## 5. TUI and OpenTUI (Entire vs Doraval render/clack)

### Does Entire use OpenTUI?

**No.** Grep over `/tmp/entire-cli-research` for `opentui` / `@opentui` / `OpenTUI`: zero hits. `go.mod` requires Charm, not OpenTUI. `CLAUDE.md` L7: “CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh”.

### What Entire’s TUI actually does

Two layers:

1. **Prompts (huh).** Confirm, select, multi-select, text. Wrapped in `uiform.New` / `NewAccessibleForm` so `ACCESSIBLE` switches to simpler text. Used by `enable`, `clean`, `session` pickers, `repo` wizards, `attach`. Source: `uiform/uiform.go`; `setup.go` `hookAgentOptions`; `sessions.go` MultiSelect; `resume_picker.go`.

2. **Full-screen apps (Bubble Tea).** `activity` (default TTY), `search` (no-query TTY), `recap`, `dispatch`, `investigate` live view, `experts --tui` (opt-in). These are dashboards / browsers over hosted session data. Not one-shot CLI prompts.

CLAUDE.md L766–814 is the important rule: **do not hide useful output behind a TUI.** Every TUI path must have list+show, a flag, or a text/JSON fallback. `experts --tui` is called out as safe because it is opt-in and non-TTY is plain text.

`CanPromptInteractively` (`interactive.go`): off in `go test`, `CI`, agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`), and when `/dev/tty` is raw (lazygit parent). Doraval already skips clack when stdin/stderr are not TTY (`prompt.ts`, `shouldConfirmScan`, `shouldAskReviewLimit`). Doraval does not special-case those agent env vars.

### What OpenTUI actually provides

From https://opentui.com/ and https://opentui.com/docs/:

- Native Zig core + TypeScript bindings. Flexbox (Yoga). Component tree.
- Packages: `@opentui/core` (imperative), `@opentui/react`, `@opentui/solid`, plus keymap / qrcode / ssh / three.
- Powers **OpenCode**, not Entire.
- License: MIT (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anomalyco/opentui/main/LICENSE). Official repo is [anomalyco/opentui](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui) (site still mentions sst in older links).

Components (https://opentui.com/docs/components/): Text, Box, Input, Textarea, Select, TabSelect, Slider, ScrollBox, Code, Markdown, Diff, TextTable, Image, QR, embedded terminal. **No Confirm. No Spinner.** That is a full-screen app kit, not a clack replacement.

Runtime (https://opentui.com/docs/getting-started/runtime-support/): Bun ≥ 1.3.0 (Doraval already requires this). Node.js “26.4.0 exactly” + `--experimental-ffi`. Native optionalDeps per platform (same pattern as Doraval’s own binaries). Adding `@opentui/core` is a new native dep + platform packages.

Leftover in this tree: `node_modules/@opentui/core@0.4.2` and `core-darwin-x64`. **Not** in `package.json` `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. A prior look only. Do not treat as adopted.

### Doraval today

| Piece | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `@clack/prompts` | confirm / select / text / password / spinner / multiselect. Already in `package.json`. |
| `src/cli/prompt.ts` | text + select; non-TTY returns fallback; chrome on stderr |
| scan, review, fix, reconcile, config, rules, bump, memory/* | clack for TTY gates |
| `memory/stash-picker.ts` | clack multiselect (cap 20) or optional `fzf` |
| `src/cli/render/backend.ts` | `RenderBackend` interface: write/info/dim/heading/success/warn/fail + `destroy()` |
| `render/text-backend.ts` | the only implementation; human UI on stderr |
| `render/index.ts` | “Text-only since the OpenTUI stack was removed — the indirection stays so exit.ts and out.ts keep a single seam.” |
| `render/exit.ts` | destroy backend then exit; backstop on `process.exit` |

`backend.ts` comment: “keep this seam; a second (TUI/dashboard) backend was removed and may return as dora ui.” That is a leftover from a removed dashboard, not a planned OpenTUI adapter. Commands use `ui.*` from `out.ts`. They never call the interface. A second backend would have to reimplement line-oriented helpers (`heading`, `failItem`), not OpenTUI’s box/flex tree. **This is a text seam, not a TUI seam.**

### Rank (YAGNI)

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Stay on clack | **Yes.** Confirm/select/spinner/multiselect already match every Doraval TTY gate. |
| OpenTUI for one surface | **No.** Scan table, review findings, reconcile picker, stash picker are not worse than Entire’s huh pickers in a way OpenTUI would fix. OpenTUI has no confirm/spinner. It is the wrong layer. |
| Skip TUI entirely | **Yes for dashboards.** Entire’s Bubble Tea views are activity/search/recap over hosted sessions. Doraval has no equivalent command. A `dora ui` dashboard is speculative. |

**OpenTUI verdict:** do not add `@opentui/*`. Entire does not use it. It is a full-app kit. Clack + `text-backend` already cover scan / review / fix / reconcile / stash. If a later command needs a full-screen browser, that is Adapt and a new dep — not Copy now.

`entire mcp` is **hidden**. Read-only. Two tools: `agent_help`, `entire_status`. Same live renderers as the CLI. JSON-RPC stdio. Source: `mcp.go` L20–27, L191–202.

Doraval already has the agent machine manifest (`src/cli/capabilities.ts`, early-exit in `index.ts`). Banner on stderr for humans. JSON on stdout. Exit 0.

The research note is at [`docs/research-notes/47-entire-cli-ux.md`](docs/research-notes/47-entire-cli-ux.md).

I checked the live `entire --help` on this machine (v0.10.1). The opener and the grouped command list match the note.

**Related skills if you want this built later:** `cli-developer` (help and errors). Do not use `opentui` for this. The note says to skip that library.

---

## OpenTUI first

Entire does **not** use OpenTUI.

Entire is Go. It uses Cobra for commands. It uses Charm `huh` for prompts. It uses Bubble Tea for full-screen views.

OpenTUI is a Zig + TypeScript kit. OpenCode uses it. Doraval can use it with no Entire dependency.

Do **not** add `@opentui/*`.

Why:

- OpenTUI is a full-screen app kit. It has boxes, images, and 3D. It has no confirm and no spinner.
- Doraval already uses `@clack/prompts` for every TTY gate.
- We already removed the OpenTUI stack. `src/cli/render/` is a text seam, not a TUI seam.
- The CLI plan already parked TUI. `dora ui` is reserved for a future web dashboard.

`@opentui/core` in `node_modules` is leftover. It is not in `package.json`.

---

## What Entire does well

`entire --help` starts with a first command: `entire enable`, then `entire agent add <name>`.

The command list is grouped: Setup, Sessions, Account, Control Plane.

Per-command `--help` has examples.

`entire agent-help` is a live map for agents. `entire status` points at it.

Every TUI path has a text or JSON fallback.

---

## What Doraval already does better

Keep these.

| Area | Why keep ours |
| --- | --- |
| Exit codes `0 / 1 / 2` | Entire only uses `0 / 1`. |
| `guidedError` + `Next:` | Entire prints one line, or dumps usage. |
| Human UI on stderr | Entire puts pretty text on stdout. |
| `--format json` + `--ci` | Entire `--json` is per-command only. |
| Completions on `--help` | Entire hides `completion`. |
| Bare `dora` = scan | Entire bare starts a setup wizard in an unset repo. |
| No hook writes | `entire enable --yes` writes hook files for every agent. That dirties git. Confirmed in their source. |

---

## Copy now (small PRs)

Same first two items as note 46. Entire agrees.

1. Add a short **Start here** on `dora --help`. Name `dora review --quick` and bare `dora`. Entire’s grouped help is about 65 lines. That is the ceiling. Do not grow past it.

2. Add examples and exit codes `0 / 1 / 2` to `review`, `fix`, and `scan` `--help`.

3. Group the COMMANDS list. Put primary verbs first. Put `bump` / `update` / `providers` on a tooling line.

4. Add one dim line on scan: `Agents: dora --capabilities`. Entire’s `status` footer does this for `agent-help`. Do not add `dora agent-help`.

---

## Skip

- OpenTUI, Bubble Tea, or any `dora ui` TUI.
- `dora enable` hook injection.
- `dora doctor` (theirs repairs stuck sessions and hook drift).
- Account, login, org, repo, checkpoints.
- MCP in this binary.
- Auto version-check after every command.

I did not change product code. Say if you want PR 1 (the `--help` Start here). Notes 46 and 47 both point at that same first cut.

FileContent.content:
1→---
name: doraval
description: "Verify agent-context quality with the `dora` CLI. Whenever you author or edit a skill (SKILL.md), plugin, rule, or agent config, run dora to check it before reporting the work done. Also use when the user asks to check, diagnose, fix, or clean up agent context across Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, or Grok. Not for ordinary source-code edits."
---

# doraval

You run `dora`. It is the verification gate on agent context: Skills, Rules, plugins, and Memory files.

10→Treat the exit code as truth. Do not report done while the code is `1` or `2`.

If `dora` is not on `PATH`, run `npx @hacksmith/doraval` in its place.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | clean | Only then report done |
| `1` | issues found | Fix or surface to the user. Do not report done |
20→| `2` | could not run | Report the failure and why. Do not claim a pass |

`--deep` Review exits `2` when no Judge is available. That is "could not run the tier you required," not clean.

## First Review

Surface Findings before JSON, LLM, or CI flags:

```bash
dora review --quick
30→```

`--quick` is structure + heuristics. No Judge. No LLM wait.

After you edit one artifact, pass its path:

```bash
dora review --quick <path>
```

40→`<path>` is the Skill directory (the folder that holds `SKILL.md`), a plugin root, or `.` for the workspace.

If Review finds more than 10 artifacts, it may ask how many to grade. Pass a path or `--all` so it does not prompt.

## Then JSON

Add `--format json` when you will branch on fields, not on a table:

```bash
dora review --quick --format json
50→```

In CI or a non-interactive subagent, add `--ci` (implies `--format json`).

Require the Judge only after a `--quick` pass is clean:

```bash
dora review --deep <path>
```

60→`--deep` exits `2` if no Judge is available. JSON keys and how to branch: [`references/output.md`](references/output.md).

## The loop

The gate is Review. Do not skip it.

1. **Review.** Run `dora review --quick` (or `dora review --quick <path>` after an edit). Read Findings. Read the exit code. Do not report done on `1` or `2`.
2. **Author** the Skill, Rule, or plugin if the user asked you to write one.
3. **Fix mechanical issues.** Preview, then apply without a TTY prompt:

70→   ```bash
   dora fix <path> --dry-run
   dora fix <path> --yes
   ```

   `--yes` applies only mechanical fixes (frontmatter, formatting, missing fields). Never run bare `dora fix`. It prompts and hangs.
4. **Judgement fixes.** Anything `--yes` cannot apply comes from `dora fix <path> --brief`. Hand-edit those. Do not wait for `--yes` to do judgement work.
5. **Re-verify.** After every fix or hand-edit, run `dora review --quick <path>` again. The gate is passed only when the exit code is `0`.
6. **Delegated Judge.** If a later Review (without `--quick`) shows LLM as `via delegated` (JSON `method: "delegated"`), dora handed you the rubric. Read the `JUDGE THIS` prompt. Evaluate the Skill against it. Fix findings before you report done. Done means mechanical tiers are clean and delegated judgment is complete.
7. **Memory — only with user intent.** When the user states a durable rule to enforce:
80→
   ```bash
   dora memory add "<rule>" --weight <1-10>
   ```

   Weight is priority (1–10, default 5). `≥ 7` is a hard rule (enforced in Review). Do not invent memories from your own inferences.

   To write hard rules into `AGENTS.md`, run `dora memory promote --dry-run`, then `dora memory promote --yes` only when the user wants that. Never run bare `promote`. It prompts.
8. **Contradictions.** If Review or Scan reports a cross-agent conflict, run `dora reconcile --dry-run` and ask the user. Never run bare `reconcile`. Use `--apply` only after the user confirms.

90→## When to reach for each verb

| Moment | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Entering a repo with agent context you did not write | `dora review --quick` |
| Just wrote or edited a Skill, Rule, or plugin | `dora review --quick <path>` |
| Branch on fields | add `--format json` |
| CI / non-interactive subagent | add `--ci` |
| Mechanical errors in Findings | `dora fix <path> --dry-run`, then `--yes` |
| User states a durable rule | `dora memory add "<rule>" --weight <1-10>` |
100→| Two agents disagree | `dora reconcile --dry-run`, then ask the user |
| Fast workspace check (no Review) | `dora --yes` (bare Scan; `--yes` skips the TTY confirm) |

## Constraints

You run in a loop that cannot answer TTY prompts.

| Command | Job | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `dora memory` | principles + stashed artifacts (see above) | sole surviving path — see below |
| `dora bump` | version bumps across plugin.json + marketplace.json | unchanged; **amended:** wants interactive discover-manifests → multiselect → confirm (B40) |
| `dora sessions` | list sessions per agent; `show` = tool calls, tokens, skills invoked | new in v1.5 (B item 29); **amended:** wants drill-down (B40) |
| `dora config` | read/write `~/.doraval/config.yml` | unchanged; **amended:** wants interactive + human table + `--format json` (B37) |
| `dora update` | self-update + refresh the agent capability matrix | extended |
| `dora completion` | bash/zsh/fish completions | unchanged |
| `dora ui` | web dashboard | parked, kept for the future |
330→| `dora providers` | packaging/spec reference table only | **Q1 → A (2026-07-14):** not repo support — bare `dora` owns Agent surfaces |

Removed entirely: `dora init` (auto-detection + lazy memory setup replaced it), `validate`, `check`, `eval`, `evals`, `judge`, `skill lint`, `drift`, `<provider>` groups (`claude`/`cursor`/`codex`/`copilot` — **Q2 2026-07-14 hard delete**; use `dora new --for <agent>` and top-level `dora bump` only; B38 demotion superseded).

**Breaking, amended after dogfood (2026-07-09):** `dora journal` is now on this removed list too — **hard removal, not a rename.** Earlier plan text ("renamed to `memory`") undersold this; the two commands shipped side by side and dogfood (F14) escalated to a full breaking kill with migration. See B33.

## A5. For coding agents

dora treats coding agents as first-class users. The JSON contract **is** the SDK — there is deliberately no importable library.

340→The contract:

| Concern | Guarantee |
|---|---|
| Discovery | `dora --capabilities` → full command manifest: args, flags, **output schemas**, **example invocations**, exit codes. **Amended after dogfood (2026-07-09):** humans hit this unlabeled and got a wall of schema — root `--help` and the flag itself need an audience label. See B39. |
| Output | every command supports `--format json`; data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr |
| Prompts | nothing blocks on stdin when `!isTTY`; `--yes` pre-approves |
| Exit codes | `0` clean · `1` issues found · `2` could not run (internal error or missing prerequisite) |
| Stability | JSON shapes are versioned in the capabilities manifest; breaking shape changes bump them |

## 8. Skip, revisited: postponed vs dropped

“Skip” in §7 meant **not this pass**. It did not mean “never ship.” #26 itself says “this pass” for `skills get` and the stub ([note 45](./45-agent-browser-docs-bar.md) §7 / §8).

Three labels:

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Postponed** | Idea may return. Do the cheaper substitute first. |
| **Form dropped, idea kept** | Do not copy their shape. A Doraval-shaped version can still land. |
| **Dropped** | Wrong product. Reopen only if the product changes. |

| Item | Label | Cheaper substitute today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dora skills get` + hidden stub | Postponed | Full shipped skill + `dora <cmd> --help` + `--capabilities` |
| `dora doctor` | Form dropped, idea kept | Bare `dora` (scan) + `dora update` + `platform-install.ts` |
| MCP in this binary | Postponed | Agents exec `dora`; JSON contract **is** the SDK ([EXCEPTIONAL-CLI-PLAN](../EXCEPTIONAL-CLI-PLAN.md) A5) |
| 390-line `--help` catalog | Form dropped, idea kept | 32-line Reader help now; paste catalog on README / `/commands` (note 45 T3) |
| `--json` alias | Postponed | `--format json` + `--ci` |
| Color off by default | Postponed | picocolors + TTY + `NO_COLOR`; `--ci` skips pretty |
| Browser sessions / `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` | Dropped | `dora sessions` is a different object (transcripts) |
| `batch` | Form dropped, idea kept | `dora review --all`; shell `&&` |
| `@eN` refs | Form dropped, idea kept | Public rule codes `R0xx` on review lines (`review.ts` `publicRuleCode`) |
| Chrome / headed / CDP / snapshots / daemon `&&` | Dropped | None. Wrong product. |

### 8.1 `dora skills get` + hidden stub — postponed

**What they have.** `npx skills add` installs a 51-line stub (`hidden: true`). The stub says: run `agent-browser skills get core` before any command. The CLI prints a 516-line workflow that matches the binary. `--full` appends `references/` ([note 45](./45-agent-browser-docs-bar.md) §5; `cli/src/skills.rs`).

**Why #26 said no this pass.** Doraval already ships one full Runner skill (`skills/doraval/SKILL.md`, ~119 lines). A stub + `skills get` is a second distribution path. We would have to keep the stub empty and move the workflow into the binary.

**Pros if we do it later**

- The workflow always matches the installed binary. `npx skills add` cannot go stale across releases.
- Progressive disclosure: short stub in the agent’s skill list, full guide on demand. Their `--full` keeps the encyclopedia out of the first load.
- `--help` can stay Reader-short and still teach agents “run this one command.”

**Cons**

- Two files, two voices, a lockstep rule. Their `AGENTS.md` already pays that tax.
- Extra hop: every session starts with `skills get` before `dora review --quick`. That fights CONTEXT.md’s first loop.
- We already have three teacher surfaces: the shipped skill, `--help`, `--capabilities`. A fourth splits the story.
- Binary-bundled markdown is a new packaging concern (compile-in vs extra files next to the binary).

**Reopen when** any of these is true:

1. Users install the skill once and then upgrade only the CLI, and agents follow stale steps.
2. The shipped skill grows past ~one screen and agents stop reading it (their split exists because 516 + 26 KB refs is too big for `npx skills add`).
3. We ship more than one Doraval skill (review vs memory vs rules) and need a directory the CLI can serve.

**Do first:** finish `--capabilities` and put examples on `review` / `fix` / `scan` `--help` (§7 items 2 and 4). That is the same “CLI teaches the agent” job, without a new verb.

### 8.2 `dora doctor` — form dropped, idea kept

**What they have.** `doctor [--fix] [--json] [--quick] [--offline]`. Checks Chrome-for-Testing, daemon sockets, encryption key, live launch. `--fix` is opt-in and destructive (`cli/src/doctor/mod.rs`; site `/installation` § Doctor).

**Why we said no.** Doraval has no browser, no daemon, no key. A clone of their checks is empty.

**The idea that remains.** One verb that answers “why can’t this run?” Distinct from “what is wrong with my skills?” Scan mixes both: artifact health **and** Intelligence / `platform-install`. Entire’s doctor is a third shape (stuck sessions + hook drift) — also not ours ([note 47](./47-entire-cli-ux.md) §4).

**Pros if we add a Doraval-shaped doctor later**

- Scan stays “repo health.” Doctor stays “runtime health”: missing optionalDep, no judge for `--deep`, bad `~/.doraval/config.yml`, stale binary.
- `--fix` can be narrow (reinstall hint, rewrite completions, reset config). Scan should not write.
- Agents get a dedicated exit-2 explainer.

**Cons**

- Second health verb. Users will not know `dora` vs `dora doctor`.
- Scan already prints Intelligence + install hints (`platform-install.ts`). `dora update` already covers upgrade.
- Empty `--fix` is worse than no command.

**Reopen when** support cost is “I ran `dora review --deep` and got exit 2 / stub binary / no judge” and scan does not name the next command in one line. Until then, put those lines on scan, not a new verb.

### 8.3 MCP in this binary — postponed

**What they have.** `agent-browser mcp` is stdio JSON-RPC. Tools re-invoke the same binary with `--json` (`cli/src/mcp.rs` L1–7). `AGENTS.md` requires CLI/MCP parity on the same PR. Entire’s MCP is hidden and only exports `agent_help` + `entire_status` ([note 47](./47-entire-cli-ux.md) §6).

**Why we said no.** Doraval is one-shot. Agents already run `dora`. Plan A5: the JSON contract **is** the SDK. There is no importable library on purpose.

**Pros if we add it later**

- Hosts that prefer MCP tools over shell (Desktop, some IDEs) get typed tools without quoting flags.
- Structured args beat `dora review --quick --format json --fail-on warning`.
- We could start tiny, Entire-style: two tools (`capabilities`, `review_quick`). Not full CLI parity.

**Cons**

- Parity tax. Every new flag becomes two surfaces. AB made that a hard rule because they felt the drift.
- Two SDKs. A5 said one: `--format json` + `--capabilities`.
- MCP is long-lived stdio. Our commands are not a session. We gain little of what AB’s daemon MCP is for.
- Auth, transport, and tool-list versioning are new product.

**Reopen when** a real host cannot exec `dora` (or users ask). If we do it, start with two read-only tools. Do not promise full parity.

### 8.4 390-line `--help` catalog — form dropped, idea kept

**What they have.** `print_help()` is ~390 lines. Same groups as README and `/commands`. Third encyclopedia. CHANGELOG `#1251` only moved “Start here” to the top; they kept the catalog.

**Why we said no for top-level `--help`.** CONTEXT.md: top-level help is Reader. 32 lines is the right size. Test pin: root blurbs stay short (`test/cli.test.ts`).

**The idea that remains.** A pasteable verb catalog. Note 45 T3 already parked that on **README + site `/commands`**, not in the binary.

**Pros of a long `--help` later**

- An agent with only the binary still sees every verb.
- One file to grep. No site fetch.

**Cons**

- Drift with README and `/commands` (they hand-sync; #26 accepted drift for docs, not a fourth copy).
- Reader `--help` becomes a man page. That is the AB failure mode.
- Citty does not print a custom catalog without forking help.

**Reopen when** we generate the catalog from one source (command-tree / capabilities) **and** still keep top-level `--help` short. Until then: short help + grouped names + examples on subcommands. Put the long paste list on the site.

### 8.5 `--json` alias — postponed

**What they have.** Global `--json` / `AGENT_BROWSER_JSON`. Entire: per-command `--json`.

**Why we said no.** `--format json` is explicit (table | json). `--ci` implies json. The skill already teaches `--format json`.

**Pros**

- Agents guess `--json` first. One alias is cheap.
- Matches AB, Entire, and many CLIs.

**Cons**

- Two flags for one mode. Docs and capabilities must list both.
- `--format table` has no counterpart if `--json` is the only short form.

**Reopen when** we see agents (or issues) passing `--json` and citty rejecting it. Implementation is a citty alias on the existing `format` / a boolean that `resolveOutputMode` already understands. Do not change the JSON error channel (keep stderr).

### 8.6 Color off by default — postponed

**What they have.** Color off unless `AGENT_BROWSER_COLOR=1`. `NO_COLOR` wins (`cli/src/color.rs`). Entire: color on TTY, `ACCESSIBLE` kills TUI, `NO_COLOR` wins.

**Why we said no.** Top-level Doraval is Reader. Color on TTY is the human default. `--ci` / non-TTY already skip pretty.

**Pros**

- Agent transcripts stay free of ANSI.
- Safer when a host forgets to set `NO_COLOR` but still captures TTY.

**Cons**

- Humans on a TTY get a dull scan. That is the default path.
- We already respect `NO_COLOR` and non-TTY via picocolors.

**Reopen when** agents paste colored scan/review tables into sessions and it hurts. Prefer `NO_COLOR` / `--ci` docs in the skill over flipping the default.

### 8.7 Browser sessions / `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` — dropped

**What they have.** Isolated browser daemon. Default session is shared and called dangerous (`skill-data/core/SKILL.md` § Always use your own session).

**Why dropped.** Different object. `dora sessions` lists coding-agent transcripts for the review evidence tier. There is no Doraval daemon to isolate.

**Reopen only if** we grow a long-lived process (a real `dora ui` server, or a review cache daemon). That is a product change, not a flag.

### 8.8 `batch` — form dropped, idea kept

**What they have.** `batch [--bail] ["cmd" …]` runs several browser commands in one process so the daemon stays up (CHANGELOG `#865`; `print_help()` Batch).

**Why the form is wrong.** We have no daemon. Shell `&&` is enough for `review` then `fix`.

**The idea that remains.** One process, many artifacts. We already have `dora review --all`.

**Pros of a later `dora batch`**

- Avoid repeated Bun/binary startup if someone scripts 20 reviews.
- `--bail` is a clear CI story.

**Cons**

- A second way to say `--all` / a shell loop.
- Startup is not measured as a problem.

**Reopen when** we measure startup (cli-developer target <50 ms) and a loop of `dora review <path>` is slow enough to care. Until then: `--all` and the shell.

### 8.9 `@eN` refs — form dropped, idea kept

**What they have.** `snapshot -i` prints `@e1`, `@e2`. The next command is `click @e2`. Refs are the product.

**Why the form is wrong.** We do not snapshot a page.

**The idea that remains.** Short stable IDs in output so the next command can point at a row. We already print `R014` on coded findings (`review.ts` `publicRuleCode`). Scan uses `E-SCAN-*`.

**Pros of later finding refs**

- `dora fix @R014` or `dora review --only R014` without path-guessing.
- Agents stop quoting whole finding sentences.

**Cons**

- IDs must be stable across runs or they lie.
- Uncoded findings have no `R0xx` today. Inventing `@f3` that shifts when the list changes is worse than no ref.

**Reopen when** agents cannot address one finding in `fix` / `--brief` without re-running review and grepping. Do it as **rule codes and finding ids we already own**, not `@eN` syntax.

### 8.10 Dropped for real (do not reopen as CLI UX)

Chrome-for-Testing, `headed`, CDP, snapshots, daemon `&&` chaining, `dora install` as a Chrome download. These are the browser product. `dora update` already matches their `upgrade`.

| **Form dropped, idea kept** | Do not copy their shape. A Doraval-shaped version can still land. |
| **Dropped** | Wrong product. Reopen only if the product changes. |

| Item | Label | Cheaper substitute today |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `--json` alias | Postponed | `--format json` + `--ci` |

| `batch` | Form dropped, idea kept | `dora review --all`; shell `&&` |
| `@eN` refs | Form dropped, idea kept | Public rule codes `R0xx` on review lines (`review.ts` `publicRuleCode`) |

### 8.1 `dora skills get` + hidden stub — postponed

**What they have.** `npx skills add` installs a 51-line stub (`hidden: true`). The stub says: run `agent-browser skills get core` before any command. The CLI prints a 516-line workflow that matches the binary. `--full` appends `references/` ([note 45](./45-agent-browser-docs-bar.md) §5; `cli/src/skills.rs`).

**Why #26 said no this pass.** Doraval already ships one full Runner skill (`skills/doraval/SKILL.md`, ~119 lines). A stub + `skills get` is a second distribution path. We would have to keep the stub empty and move the workflow into the binary.

**Pros if we do it later**

- The workflow always matches the installed binary. `npx skills add` cannot go stale across releases.
- Progressive disclosure: short stub in the agent’s skill list, full guide on demand. Their `--full` keeps the encyclopedia out of the first load.
- `--help` can stay Reader-short and still teach agents “run this one command.”

**Cons**

- Two files, two voices, a lockstep rule. Their `AGENTS.md` already pays that tax.
- Extra hop: every session starts with `skills get` before `dora review --quick`. That fights CONTEXT.md’s first loop.
- We already have three teacher surfaces: the shipped skill, `--help`, `--capabilities`. A fourth splits the story.
- Binary-bundled markdown is a new packaging concern (compile-in vs extra files next to the binary).

**Reopen when** any of these is true:

1. Users install the skill once and then upgrade only the CLI, and agents follow stale steps.
2. The shipped skill grows past ~one screen and agents stop reading it (their split exists because 516 + 26 KB refs is too big for `npx skills add`).
3. We ship more than one Doraval skill (review vs memory vs rules) and need a directory the CLI can serve.

**Do first:** finish `--capabilities` and put examples on `review` / `fix` / `scan` `--help` (§7 items 2 and 4). That is the same “CLI teaches the agent” job, without a new verb.

**What they have.** `doctor [--fix] [--json] [--quick] [--offline]`. Checks Chrome-for-Testing, daemon sockets, encryption key, live launch. `--fix` is opt-in and destructive (`cli/src/doctor/mod.rs`; site `/installation` § Doctor).

**Why we said no.** Doraval has no browser, no daemon, no key. A clone of their checks is empty.

**The idea that remains.** One verb that answers “why can’t this run?” Distinct from “what is wrong with my skills?” Scan mixes both: artifact health **and** Intelligence / `platform-install`. Entire’s doctor is a third shape (stuck sessions + hook drift) — also not ours ([note 47](./47-entire-cli-ux.md) §4).

**Pros if we add a Doraval-shaped doctor later**

- Scan stays “repo health.” Doctor stays “runtime health”: missing optionalDep, no judge for `--deep`, bad `~/.doraval/config.yml`, stale binary.
- `--fix` can be narrow (reinstall hint, rewrite completions, reset config). Scan should not write.
- Agents get a dedicated exit-2 explainer.

**Cons**

- Second health verb. Users will not know `dora` vs `dora doctor`.
- Scan already prints Intelligence + install hints (`platform-install.ts`). `dora update` already covers upgrade.
- Empty `--fix` is worse than no command.

**Reopen when** support cost is “I ran `dora review --deep` and got exit 2 / stub binary / no judge” and scan does not name the next command in one line. Until then, put those lines on scan, not a new verb.

### 8.3 MCP in this binary — postponed

**What they have.** `agent-browser mcp` is stdio JSON-RPC. Tools re-invoke the same binary with `--json` (`cli/src/mcp.rs` L1–7). `AGENTS.md` requires CLI/MCP parity on the same PR. Entire’s MCP is hidden and only exports `agent_help` + `entire_status` ([note 47](./47-entire-cli-ux.md) §6).

**Why we said no.** Doraval is one-shot. Agents already run `dora`. Plan A5: the JSON contract **is** the SDK. There is no importable library on purpose.

**Pros if we add it later**

- Hosts that prefer MCP tools over shell (Desktop, some IDEs) get typed tools without quoting flags.
- Structured args beat `dora review --quick --format json --fail-on warning`.
- We could start tiny, Entire-style: two tools (`capabilities`, `review_quick`). Not full CLI parity.

**Cons**

- Parity tax. Every new flag becomes two surfaces. AB made that a hard rule because they felt the drift.
- Two SDKs. A5 said one: `--format json` + `--capabilities`.
- MCP is long-lived stdio. Our commands are not a session. We gain little of what AB’s daemon MCP is for.
- Auth, transport, and tool-list versioning are new product.

**Reopen when** a real host cannot exec `dora` (or users ask). If we do it, start with two read-only tools. Do not promise full parity.

**What they have.** `print_help()` is ~390 lines. Same groups as README and `/commands`. Third encyclopedia. CHANGELOG `#1251` only moved “Start here” to the top; they kept the catalog.

**The idea that remains.** A pasteable verb catalog. Note 45 T3 already parked that on **README + site `/commands`**, not in the binary.

**Pros of a long `--help` later**

- An agent with only the binary still sees every verb.
- One file to grep. No site fetch.

**Cons**

- Reader `--help` becomes a man page. That is the AB failure mode.
- Citty does not print a custom catalog without forking help.

### 8.5 `--json` alias — postponed

**What they have.** Global `--json` / `AGENT_BROWSER_JSON`. Entire: per-command `--json`.

**Why we said no.** `--format json` is explicit (table | json). `--ci` implies json. The skill already teaches `--format json`.

**Pros**

- Agents guess `--json` first. One alias is cheap.
- Matches AB, Entire, and many CLIs.

**Cons**

- Two flags for one mode. Docs and capabilities must list both.
- `--format table` has no counterpart if `--json` is the only short form.

**Pros**

- Agent transcripts stay free of ANSI.
- Safer when a host forgets to set `NO_COLOR` but still captures TTY.

**Cons**

- Humans on a TTY get a dull scan. That is the default path.
- We already respect `NO_COLOR` and non-TTY via picocolors.

**Reopen when** agents paste colored scan/review tables into sessions and it hurts. Prefer `NO_COLOR` / `--ci` docs in the skill over flipping the default.

**Reopen only if** we grow a long-lived process (a real `dora ui` server, or a review cache daemon). That is a product change, not a flag.

Their doctor checks Chrome, a daemon, and an encryption key. A copy of that is empty.
